audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0,46%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0,25%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 è in calo dell'0,14% a sette mila quattrocentonovantotto punti. Il VIX è in rialzo del 7,57% a diciassette virgola novanta, segnale di avversione al rischio. Il Dollar Index è in lieve calo dello 0,08% a centouno virgola zero sei. L'oro è in ribasso dell'1,24% a quattro mila novantacinque dollari l'oncia. Il Brent scende dell'8,15% a ottantasei virgola quaranta dollari al barile. Il rendimento del US 10Y è in rialzo dello 0,63% a quattro virgola sessantacinque per cento. Il TLT 20Y è in calo dello 0,26% a ottantatré virgola quaranta quattro. Il BTP 10Y resta stabile al tre virgola settantatré per cento. Il FTSE MIB è in ribasso dell'1,51% a cinquantunomila novecentonovantaquattro punti. Il STOXX 600 è in calo dello 0,73% a sessanta tre virgola novanta otto punti.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la NATO Summit inizia oggi a Washington, con discussioni su spese difensive europee; le tensioni tra Pechino e Taipei si intensificano, Pechino esplora nuovi concetti di guerra cognitiva. Questi sviluppi mantengono alta l'incertezza sui mercati emergenti.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi. Le nuove proposte di banconote in euro saranno presentate più tardi, ma non influiscono sui mercati nella giornata.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin registra una lieve flessione dello 0,67 percento, attestandosi a sessantacinquemila quattrocentododici dollari. Gli ETF mostrano un afflusso netto di $+203,2 milioni, segnale di interesse istituzionale nonostante la pressione di petrolio e tassi in rialzo. Inoltre, il mercato osserva notizie contrastanti: la BancaStato svizzera lancia una piattaforma regolamentata, mentre gli investitori monitorano l’impatto dei tassi sui prezzi. Per quanto riguarda gli altcoin, Ethereum rimane pressoché invariato con una variazione di 0,01 percento a millenovecentiquindici dollari, Solana guadagna 0,07 percento a settantasette dollari e Binance Coin avanza dello 0,25 percento a cinquecentosessantanove dollari; nessuno supera la soglia del due percento, quindi non emergono movimenti rilevanti. Sentiment del mercato: l’indice Fear & Greed segna trenta‑uno, classe paura, suggerendo cautela tra gli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed up 0.46%, Shanghai up 0.25%. That suggests a weak open for European markets.

The S&P 500 is down 0.14% at 7,498 points. The VIX is up 7.57% at 17.9, a sign of risk aversion. The Dollar Index is slightly down 0.08% at 101.06. Gold is down 1.24% at $4,095 per ounce. Brent falls 8.15% at $86.4 per barrel. The US 10Y yield is up 0.63% at 4.65 percent. The TLT 20Y is down 0.26% at 83.44. The BTP 10Y remains flat at 3.73 percent. The FTSE MIB is down 1.51% at 51,994 points. The STOXX 600 is down 0.73% at 63.98 points.

On the geopolitical front, the NATO Summit kicks off today in Washington, with talks on European defence spending; tensions between Beijing and Taipei are intensifying, Beijing is exploring new concepts of cognitive warfare. These developments keep uncertainty high for emerging markets.

No major macro data scheduled today. New euro banknote proposals will be presented later, but they do not affect markets today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin slips 0.67 percent, sitting at $65,412. ETFs show a net inflow of $+203.2 million, a sign of institutional interest despite oil and rate pressure. Meanwhile, the market sees mixed news: the Swiss State Bank launches a regulated platform, while investors watch rate impacts on prices. Regarding altcoins, Ethereum is essentially flat with a 0.01 percent change at $1,915, Solana gains 0.07 percent at $77, and Binance Coin advances 0.25 percent at $569; none break the two‑percent threshold, so no notable moves emerge. Market sentiment: the Fear & Greed index reads 31, fear class, suggesting caution among investors.

No macro data on the agenda today. For deeper coverage of today's topics, visit our platform for the full articles in the Featured Stories section. Thank you for listening and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: ‘Structural divergence’ in China’s economy exposes a growing problem
articles.snippet: ‘Structural divergence’ in China’s economy exposes a growing problem Expert comment thilton.drupal 22 July 2026 Manufacturing is thriving while household spending is suffering. This seems to reflect a deliberate strategy by Beijing to maximize its geopolitical leverage. Growth suffers as a result. China’s policymakers can compete with the best when it comes to euphemism, and one new phrase worth taking note of is ‘ jiegou fenhua ’ or ‘structural divergence’ – a term the People’s Bank of China used in its July statement to describe what’s going on in the Chinese economy. What it means is that the economy is running at two different speeds. The manufacturing sector and exports are enjoying a stellar performance, while indicators of household spending and satisfaction remain in the doldrums.

articles.title: Can the world benefit from China’s quest for food security?
articles.snippet: Can the world benefit from China’s quest for food security? Expert comment jon.wallace 22 July 2026 China wants to become more self-sufficient in food. This could make it easier to fight climate change and improve nutrition worldwide, but there are also risks to global food markets. China’s remarkable economic transformation over the past four decades has sharply reduced the share of its population who are hungry – from 30 per cent in 1980 to less than 2.5 per cent today. In part that has been achieved by ensuring it has the means to buy the food and food inputs it cannot make for itself. Today China is the world’s largest agricultural importer, accounting for 60 per cent of soybean imports and 76 per cent of beef imports in 2024.
